note: The two sets are nearly identical in content: same elevations, keynote codes, drawing scales and locations, with the same two duplicated datum facts (finish floor and int. step each stated twice). A phrases the datum as 'height above ground plane', while B splits each into a bare 'height' claim and an 'elevation' claim with the condition 'relative to GROUND PLANE'. Neither set is clearly more faithful: both keep the datum somewhere in each pair, and both lose it on the other claim of the pair, so the trade-off (A's slightly vaguer binding vs B's explicit condition) nets out.
remarks: Both sets repeat the finish-floor and int.-step facts under two attribute names (elevation vs height), so each has 2 redundant claims out of 17. B's bare 'height' claims are ambiguous (could read as height of the floor/step rather than elevation above the datum); A's bare 'elevation' claims omit the datum. The keynote/spec codes (22 11 23.A2, 11 31 13.A7, 22 11 16, etc.) are bound identically in both sets to 'Water Supply System' or generic 'component' with location claims like 'right side of enclosure' that cannot be verified from the text layer alone and are quite vague; the leader-line placements are only visible in the image.
